rules.name: Ambush Tactics
rules.text: When deployed on the table, these units may start the game on Ambush. (also page 24 AoIJ)

rules.name: Assault
rules.text: This weapon suffers no penalty 'to hit' when moving and shooting. In addition, infantry models armed with an assault weapon count as having the Tough Fighters special rule (Tough Fighters: When a model with this special rule fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage)

rules.name: Battle Flag
rules.text: Any Infantry or Artillery unit within 12” and line of sight to a Battle Flag adds +1 to its morale value. Only one Battle Flag may be included in a force. In addition, if you roll 1 on the Air Strike table, the enemy cannot target a unit that is within 12” of a flag. A Battle Flag cannot be given to a unit’s leader (e.g. NCOs, officers, etc), or to a model with a Signalling Bugle.

rules.name: Behind enemy lines
rules.text: When outflanking as described on page 172, unit ignores the -1 modifier to the order test for coming onto the table.

rules.name: Bicycles
rules.text: When moving on roads, they double their Run move to 24" (cannot be used to Assault). The first time they receive any order other than Run, or if they receive a Pin marker, they dismount and abandon their bicycles for the rest of the game.

rules.name: Cavalry
rules.text: Can dismount and fight on foot as infantry, from which point none of these rules apply - need to replace mounted figures with non-mounted figures. When cavalry, moves 9" at an Advance, 18" at Run. Cannot enter buildings or board transport vehicles unless they have dismounted. Cannot gain advantages of Down, and their cover saves are always reduced by 1. Can escape as a recce vehicle (at normal speed, not double speed). Can dismount as part of Advance move - cannot remount. Can only fire pistol or carbine (treated as pistol) when mounted. While mounted, cavalry have Tough Fighters special rule (p122- When fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage). Can regroup up to 2D6" after combat.

rules.name: Fieldcraft (artillery)
rules.text: (v3 page 120) Treat rough ground as open ground instead. (AoIJ: this applies to light howitzers and light anti-tank guns too, but not to other artillery units).

rules.name: Green
rules.text: Green units are inexperienced and have a morale rating of 8. The first time the unit suffers a casualty, roll a die (after taking any morale checks caused by the attack). On a roll of a 1 the unit suffers an additional D6 pin markers and goes Down. There is no further effect. On a 2, 3, 4, or 5 the unit fights on. There is not further effect. On a 6 the unit is immediately up-rated to Regular with a morale value of 9 for the rest of the battle.

rules.name: Intelligence
rules.text: Once per game, at the beginning of any turn (as long as the Intelligence Officer is on the table), the Officer may act on intelligence gathered about the enemy force before the first die is drawn from the dice bag. Roll a D6, a Veteran Officer receives a +1 modifier on the roll, an Inexperienced one receives a -1 modifier. On a 4+, the player using this ability may choose a die from the bag for the first activation. If both players are doing this in the same turn and both succeed in this roll, the results cancel out and the dice is randomly drawn, as normal. Only one Officer in the entire force may have Intelligence training.

rules.name: Iron Discipline
rules.text: May remove 2 pin markers rather than the usual 1 if an order test is passed.

rules.name: Shin Gunto
rules.text: Any model armed with a sword (Shin Gunto) gains the Tough Fighters special rule. If the model already has the Tough Fighters special rule, it rolls an additional dice in close quarters against infantry and artillery units.

rules.name: Signaling Bugle
rules.text: All Inexperienced enemy Infantry and Artillery units within 36” of a Signalling Bugle suffer from a -1 modifier to their morale value, as long as they have no line of sight to the model carrying the Bugle. Only one Signalling Bugle may be included in a force. A Signalling Bugle cannot be given to a unit’s leader (e.g. NCOs, officers, etc), or to a model with a Battle Flag.

rules.name: SNLF Commander
rules.text: SNLF platoon commanders reduce their costs by 5pts and SNLF company commanders reduce their cost by 10pts. On the other hand, their 'You Men Snap to Action' ability (including when executing a Banzai! order) only affects other SNLF units, amphibious vehicles and all transport vehicles that are transporting at least one SNLF unit.

rules.name: Tough Fighters
rules.text: When a model with this special rule fails to damage in close quarters against enemy infantry or artillery units, it can re-roll the failed rolls to damage.

rules.name: Unpredictable
rules.text: Any time a Home Defence unit fails an orders test, roll a D6 and consult the chart below:1-2: The unit immediately goes Down, in addition it takes D3 pin markers.3-4: The unit immediately goes Down as normal.5-6: The unit immediately makes a Run order towards the nearest visible enemy unit. If this move would bring them into contact with that unit, it counts as an assault into close quarters.

armyRules.name: Death Before Dishonour
armyRules.text: All Imperial Japanese infantry and artillery units have the Fanatics special rule. In addition, they automatically pass morale checks for being assaulted by enemy tanks (note that artillery pieces are still destroyed as normal).

armyRules.name: Banzai!
armyRules.text: A Japanese Officer may be given a special Banzai! order. This counts as a "You Men Snap to Action" with the following exceptions: If the order is given successfully, assign the officer a Run order die. Then

armyRules.name: ALL
armyRules.text: infantry units within 6” that haven’t already received an order that turn are issued a Run order. Note that this includes infantry units which cannot normally assault enemies, such as those with the Fixed special rule, or the Self-defence special rule. All infantry units can and will assault into close quarters if given the opportunity (09/2026 errata). Note that, other than for the initiating officer, no order test is required for any units affected by a Banzai! order. This means that affected units execute their Run orders automatically, without any dice rolled, and as such retain any pin markers they have.

armyRules.name: Lack of Radios
armyRules.text: When you give the Command Vehicle special rule to a vehicle that does not have it in its entry for the purposes of choosing a command vehicle for an Armoured Platoon, you can give it the rule for free instead of paying the normal +10pts. If you do so, the vehicle reduces the radius of its Command Vehicle rule from 12” to 6”. This represents communication by means of flags or hand signals.
